translations.text: These are the words Moses spoke to all Israel beyond the Jordan, in the wilderness, in the Arabah opposite Suph, between Paran and Tophel, and Lebanon, Hazeroth, and Dizahab.
It is an eleven-day journey from Horeb to Mount Seir and on to Kadesh-barnea.
In the fortieth year, in the eleventh month, on the first day of the month, Moses told the Israelites everything the LORD had commanded him concerning them.
This was after he had killed Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon, and Og king of Bashan, who lived in Ashtaroth and Edrei.
Beyond the Jordan, in the land of Moab, Moses began to explain this law, saying:
“The LORD our God said to us at Horeb, ‘You have stayed at this mountain long enough.

Turn and set out, and enter the hill country of the Amorites and all its surrounding regions: the Arabah, the hill country, the lowlands, the Negev, and the seacoast—the land of the Canaanites and Lebanon—as far as the great river, the Euphrates.
See, I have placed the land before you. Go in and take possession of the land that the LORD swore to give to your fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and to their descendants after them.’
And I said to you at that time, “I cannot bear the burden of you by myself.”
The LORD your God has multiplied you, and today you are as numerous as the stars in the sky.
May the LORD, the God of your fathers, make you a thousand times as numerous as you are and bless you as he promised you.
How, then, can I bear your weight, your burdens, and your disputes by myself?
Choose for yourselves wise, discerning men who are known to your tribes, and I will appoint them as your leaders.
You answered me, ‘What you have proposed to do is good.’

So I took the heads of your tribes, wise and well-known men, and appointed them as leaders over you: leaders of thousands, leaders of hundreds, leaders of fifties, leaders of tens, and scribes for your tribes.
At that time I instructed your judges, saying to them, ‘Hear disputes among your fellow Israelites and judge fairly between a man and his fellow Israelite or the foreigner living among them.

Show no favoritism in judgment. Hear the small and the great alike. Do not be afraid of anyone, because judgment belongs to God. Bring any case that is too difficult for you to me, and let me hear it.’
At that time I instructed you about everything you were to do.

We set out from Horeb and traveled through all that great and terrifying wilderness that you saw, in the land of the hill country of the Amorites, as the LORD our God had commanded us, and we came to Kadesh-barnea.
I said to you, ‘You have reached the hill country of the Amorites, which the LORD our God is giving us.
See, the LORD your God has placed the land before you. Go up and take possession of the land, as the LORD, the God of your fathers, told you. Do not be afraid or terrified.’
Then all of you came to me and said, ‘Let us send men ahead of us to explore the land for us and bring us a report, showing us the route we should take and the towns we should enter.’
The proposal seemed good to me, so I took twelve men from among you, one man from each tribe.
They turned and went up into the hill country. They went up as far as the Valley of Eshcol and explored the land.
They took some of the land’s fruit in their hands and brought it to us. They brought us a report and said, ‘The land that the LORD our God is giving us is good.’
But you were unwilling to go up and rebelled against the command spoken by the LORD our God.
You grumbled in your tents and said, ‘Because the LORD hates us, he brought us out of Egypt to hand us over to the Amorites so that they would destroy us.’

Where are we going up? Our brothers have discouraged us and told us, “The people are greater, taller, and stronger than we are, and the cities are large and fortified up to the heavens. We also saw descendants of giants there.”
And I told you, “Do not be afraid or terrified of them.”
The Lord your God goes ahead of you, and he fights for you, just as in everything he did for you in Egypt before your eyes.
And in the wilderness you saw how the Lord your God sustained you, as a man sustains his son, throughout the land you traveled through until you came to this place.
Yet in this matter you do not trust the Lord your God,
who goes ahead of you on the way to prepare a place for you to camp, in fire at night to show you the way you should go, and in a cloud by day.
The Lord heard what you said, became angry, and swore an oath, saying,
“Not one of these men, this evil generation, will see the good land that I swore to give your ancestors,
except Caleb son of Jephunneh. He will see it, and I will give him and his children the land he walked on, because he followed the Lord wholeheartedly.”
The Lord was angry with me too because of you, and he told me, “You too will not enter there.
But Joshua son of Nun, who stands before you, will enter there. Strengthen him, because he will give it to Israel as an inheritance.
Your dependents, whom you said would become plunder, and your children, who today do not know good from evil, will enter there. I will give it to them, and they will inherit it.
But you must turn back and set out into the wilderness by the road to the Red Sea.”

You answered me, “We have sinned before the Lord our God. We will go up and fight, as the Lord our God commanded us.” Each of you armed himself with his weapons of war, and you were eager to go up into the hill country.
The Lord said to me, “Tell them, ‘Do not go up and do not fight, because I will not be among you, so that you will not be defeated before your enemies.’”
I told you, but you did not listen. You rebelled against the command from the Lord’s mouth, acted presumptuously, and went up into the hill country.
The Amorites who lived in that hill country came out against you. They chased you like bees stirred up by smoke and drove you from Seir as far as Hormah.
You sat down and wept before the Lord, but the Lord did not listen to your voice or pay attention to you.
You stayed in Rekem for many days, as long as the days you stayed there.
Then we turned back and set out into the wilderness by the road to the Red Sea, as the Lord had told me, and we went around Mount Seir for many days.
The Lord said to me,
“You have been going around this mountain long enough. Turn north.
Command the people and tell them, ‘You are passing through the territory of your relatives, the descendants of Esau, who live in Seir. They will be afraid of you. Be very careful,

and do not provoke them, because I will not give you any of their land as an inheritance, not even enough for the sole of a foot to tread on, because I have given Mount Seir to Esau as an inheritance.
Buy grain from them with silver and eat it. Buy water from them with silver as well, and drink it.’”

For the Lord your God has blessed you in all the work of your hands and has known your journey through this wilderness. For these forty years the Lord your God has been with you, and you have lacked nothing.

We passed by our relatives, the descendants of Esau, who live in Seir, leaving the road of the Arabah, Elath, and Ezion-geber. Then we turned and traveled along the road through the wilderness of Moab.
The Lord said to me, “Do not harass the Moabites or provoke them to battle, because I will not give you any of their land as a possession. I have given it to the descendants of Lot as a possession.”
The Emim lived there formerly, a great and numerous people, as tall as giants.
They are giants, and they too are counted as giants, but the Moabites call them Emim.

The Horites formerly lived in Seir, but the descendants of Esau dispossessed them, destroyed them before them, and settled in their land, just as Israel did to the land of its possession, which the Lord gave them.
“Now get up and cross the Zered Valley.” So we crossed the Zered Valley.

The time we traveled from Kadesh-barnea until we crossed the Zered Valley was thirty-eight years, until the entire generation of fighting men had perished from the camp, as the Lord had sworn to them.
The Lord’s hand was also against them, to destroy them from the camp until they were all gone.
When all the fighting men among the people had finished dying,
the Lord spoke to me and said,
“Today you are crossing into the territory of Moab and Ar.

When you approach the Ammonites, do not harass them or provoke them, because I will not give you any of the Ammonites’ land as a possession. I have given it to the descendants of Lot as a possession.”
It too is considered a land of giants. Giants formerly lived there, and the Ammonites call them Zamzummim.
They were a great and numerous people, as tall as giants. The Lord destroyed them before the Ammonites, who dispossessed them and settled in their land.
This was like what the descendants of Esau who live in Seir did: they destroyed the Horites before them, dispossessed them, and settled in their land, where they remain to this day.
As for the Avvim who lived in Hazerim as far as Gaza, the Cappadocians who came from Cappadocia destroyed them and settled in their land.
“Now get up, set out, and cross the Arnon Valley. See, I have handed over to you Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and his land. Begin to destroy him, and engage him in battle.
Today I will begin to put the fear and dread of you upon the peoples under heaven. They will hear reports of you, tremble, and be afraid of you.”
I sent messengers from the wilderness of Karmoth [?] to Sihon king of Heshbon with peaceful words, saying to him,
“Let us pass through your land. We will stay strictly on the road and will not turn aside to the right or to the left.
Sell us grain for money so that we may eat, and sell us water for money so that we may drink. Only let us pass through on foot,
as the descendants of Esau who live in Seir and the Moabites who live in Ar did for us, until we cross the Jordan into the land that the Lord our God is giving us.”

But Sihon king of Heshbon was unwilling to let us pass through his territory, because the Lord your God had hardened his spirit and made his heart stubborn, so that he might hand him over to you, as he has today.
The Lord said to me, “See, I have begun to hand Sihon and his land over to you. Begin to destroy him and take possession of his land.”
Sihon came out to meet us, he and all his people, for battle at Jahaz.
The Lord our God handed him over to us, and we struck him down, along with his sons and all his people.
We captured all his towns at that time. We completely destroyed all the towns, along with the women and families, and left no survivor among them.
We took only the livestock for ourselves as plunder, along with the spoil from the towns we had captured.
From Aroer [?], on the bank of the Arnon Valley, and the town in the valley, as far as Gilead, there was no town too strong for us. The Lord our God handed them all over to us.
But you did not approach the land of the Ammonites: all the territory beside the Jabbok Valley, the towns in the hills, and everything the Lord our God had commanded us not to approach.
We turned and went up along the road to Bashan. Og king of Bashan came out to meet us, he and all his people, for battle at Edrei.

The Lord said to me, “Do not be afraid of him, because I have handed him over to you, along with all his people and his land. Do to him as you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon.”
The Lord our God also handed over to us Og king of Bashan and all his people. We destroyed him and left him no survivor.
We captured all his cities at that time, leaving no city that we did not take from them: sixty cities, the whole region of Argob, the territory of Og’s kingdom in Bashan.
All these towns had strong walls and high gates and bars, besides the very many towns in the open country.
We destroyed them as we had done to Sihon king of Heshbon, completely destroying all his towns, along with the women and families.
We took all the livestock and the spoil of the towns for ourselves as plunder.
At that time we took the land from the two kings of the Amorites beyond the Jordan, from the Arnon Valley to Mount Hermon.
The Sidonians call Hermon Sirion, and the Amorites call it Senir.
And all the towns of the plain, all Gilead, and all Bashan as far as Salecah and Edrei—all the towns of Og’s kingdom in Bashan.

For Og king of Bashan alone remained of the remnant of the giants. His bed was an iron bed, and there it is in Rabbah of the Ammonites. It is nine cubits long and four cubits wide, measured by the cubit of the giants.
We took possession of this land at that time. From Aroer [?], on the bank of the Arnon Valley, together with half the hill country of Gilead and its towns, I gave it to Reuben and Gad.
The rest of Gilead and all Bashan, the territory of Og’s kingdom, I gave to the half-tribe of Manasseh. The whole region of Argob and all Bashan are called the land of the giants.
Jair son of Manasseh took for himself the whole region of Argob as far as the border of Geshur and Maacath. He named them after himself: Bashan and the villages of Jair, to this day.
I gave Gilead to Machir.
To Reuben and Gad I gave the territory from Gilead to the Arnon Valley, including the middle of the valley and its border, and as far as the Jabbok, the valley on the border of the Ammonites.
And the Arabah and the Jordan, with the boundary extending from Chinnereth to the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, below Ashdod and Pisgah, on the height to the east.
At that time I commanded you and said to you, “The Lord your God is giving you this land to possess. Cross over, armed, ahead of your fellow Israelites, all of you mighty warriors.”
Only leave your wives, your families, and your livestock—for I know that you have many possessions. Let them remain in your cities that I have given you.

Until the Lord gives your brothers rest as he has given you, and they too inherit the land that the Lord your God is giving you across the Jordan. Then you shall return, each to his inheritance that I have given you.
At that time I commanded Joshua and said, “Your eyes have seen everything the Lord your God did to these two kings. The Lord will do the same to all these kingdoms into which you are crossing.”
Do not be afraid of them, because the Lord your God is the one who fights for you.
At that time I pleaded before the Lord and said:

“Please, Lord God, you have begun to show your servant your greatness, your mighty hand, and your uplifted arm. For what god is there in heaven or on earth who can do deeds like yours and mighty acts like yours?
Let me now cross over and see the good land beyond the Jordan, this good hill country and Lebanon.”
The Lord was angry with me because of you and did not listen to me. The Lord said to me, “Enough! Do not speak to me again about this matter.”
“Go up to the top of the height. Lift your eyes toward the east and west, the north and south, and see it with your own eyes. But you shall not cross this Jordan.
Give Joshua his instructions, encourage him, and strengthen him, because he will cross over ahead of this people, and he will give them possession of the land that you will see.”
And we stayed in the valley opposite Beth-peor.
Now, Israel, listen to the laws and judgments that I am teaching you today to follow, so that you may live and enter and possess the land that the LORD, the God of your ancestors, is giving you.
Do not add to the commandment that I am giving you, and do not take anything away from it. Instead, keep the commandment of the LORD your God that I am giving you.
Your own eyes have seen everything that the LORD did concerning Baal-peor. For the LORD your God destroyed from among you everyone who followed Baal-peor.
But you who held fast to the LORD your God are all still alive today.
See, I have taught you laws and judgments, as the LORD my God commanded me, so that you may follow them in the land you are entering to possess.
Keep them and follow them, for this is your wisdom and understanding in the sight of the nations. They will hear all these laws and say, ‘This great nation is indeed a wise and understanding people.’
For what great nation has its god near it, as the LORD our God is whenever we call on him?
And what great nation has laws and judgments as just as this entire law that I am setting before you today?

Only be very careful and guard yourselves, so that you do not forget all the things your eyes have seen or let them leave your hearts as long as you live. Make them known to your children and your grandchildren.

On the day when you stood before the LORD your God at Horeb, the LORD said to me, ‘Gather the people before me, and I will let them hear my words, so that they may learn to fear me all the days they live on the earth, and may teach their children.’
You came near and stood at the foot of the mountain. The mountain was blazing with fire up to the heart of the heavens, with darkness, cloud, and thick gloom.
The LORD spoke with you on the mountain from within the fire. You heard the sound of words, but you saw no form—only a voice.
He made his covenant known to you and commanded you to carry out the ten commandments, and he wrote them on two stone tablets.
At that time the LORD commanded me to teach you laws and judgments, so that you would follow them in the land you are crossing over to possess.
Be very careful to guard yourselves, because you saw no form on the day the LORD spoke with you at Horeb from within the fire.
Do not corrupt yourselves by making idols and likenesses of any kind for yourselves: a likeness of a male or a female,
a likeness of any animal on the earth, a likeness of any winged bird that flies in the sky,
a likeness of anything that crawls on the ground, or a likeness of any fish in the sea beneath the earth.

And do not lift your eyes to the heavens and see the sun, the moon, the stars, and all the heavenly hosts, and be led astray into bowing down to them and serving them. The LORD your God has allotted them to all the nations under heaven. ...
But the Lord brought you near and brought you out of the iron furnace, out of Egypt, to be his people and his inheritance, as you are today.
The LORD was angry with me because of your words, and he swore that I would not cross this Jordan or enter the good land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance.
For I am going to die in this land; I will not cross this Jordan. But you will cross over and possess this good land.
Be careful not to forget the covenant of the Lord your God that he made with you, and not to make for yourselves images and likenesses of anything concerning which the Lord your God commanded you.
For the LORD your God is a consuming fire, a jealous God.

When you have children or grandchildren, and they have grown old in the land, and you corrupt yourselves by making idols and likenesses of anything, doing what is evil before the LORD your God and provoking him to anger,

I call heaven and earth to witness against you today that you will certainly perish quickly from the land you are crossing the Jordan to possess. You will not live long in it, but will certainly be destroyed.
The Lord will scatter you among the nations, and you will be left few in number among the nations where the Lord your God scatters you.
There you will serve other gods, made by human hands, of wood and stone, which cannot see or hear or eat or smell.
There you will seek the LORD your God and find him, when you search for him with all your heart and all your soul.
When you are in distress and all these things have happened to you in the latter days, you will return to the Lord your God and obey his voice.
For the Lord your God is a merciful God. He will not destroy you or abandon you, and he will not forget the covenant he swore to your ancestors.

But ask about the former days, which came before you, from the day God created human beings on the earth. Ask from one end of heaven to the other: has anything as great as this ever happened, or has anything like it ever been heard of?
Has any other people heard the voice of God speaking from within the fire, as you have heard, and survived?

Or has God ever undertaken to go and take for himself a people from within another people, through trials, signs, wonders, wars, a mighty hand, an uplifted arm, and great visions—all that the Lord your God did to the Egyptians before your eyes?
You have seen and have come to know that the Lord is God, and there is no other besides him.
From heaven he let you hear his voice to instruct you. On earth he showed you his great fire, and he let you hear his words from within the fire.
Because he loved your ancestors, he chose their descendants after them, and he himself brought you out of Egypt with great power,
to destroy before you nations greater and stronger than you, to bring you in and give you their land as an inheritance, as it is today.
Know today and take it to heart that the Lord is God in heaven above and on the earth below, and there is no other besides him.

Keep his laws and his commandments that I command you today, so that it may go well with you and your children after you, and so that you may live long in the land that the Lord your God is giving you for all time.
Then Moses set apart three towns beyond the Jordan, toward the sunrise,
so that someone who killed a neighbor unintentionally, without having hated that person previously [?], could flee there. The killer could flee to one of these towns and live.
One of them was Bezer in the wilderness, in the tableland belonging to Reuben; another was Ramoth-gilead, belonging to Gad; and Golan in Bashan, belonging to Manasseh.
This is the law that Moses set before the Israelites.
These are the testimonies, laws, and judgments that Moses spoke to the Israelites when they came out of Egypt,
beyond the Jordan, in the valley opposite Beth-peor, in the land of Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon. Moses and the Israelites killed him when they came out of Egypt.
They took possession of his land and the land of Og king of Bashan, the two kings of the Amorites beyond the Jordan, toward the sunrise,
From Aroer [?], on the bank of the Arnon Valley, as far as Mount Sirion, which is Hermon.
and all the Arabah beyond the Jordan to the east, as far as the Sea of the Arabah below Ashdod and Pisgah.
Moses summoned all Israel and said to them, “Listen, Israel, to the laws and judgments that I proclaim before you today, so that you may learn them, keep them, and carry them out.”
The Lord our God made a covenant with us at Horeb.
The Lord did not make this covenant with our ancestors, but with us, who are here today, all of us alive.
The Lord spoke with you face to face on the mountain, from within the fire.
At that time I stood between the Lord and you to make known to you the words of the Lord your God, because you were afraid of the fire and did not go up the mountain. He said:
I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
You must have no other god besides me.
You must not make for yourself any image or any likeness of anything in heaven above, on the earth below, or in the waters beneath the earth.
You must not bow down to them or worship them, for I, the Lord your God, am a jealous God, punishing children for the sins of their fathers to the third and fourth generations of those who hate me.
And I show kindness to thousands of generations, to those who love me and keep my commandments.
Do not swear falsely by the name of the Lord your God, for the Lord will not acquit anyone who swears falsely by his name.
Observe the Sabbath day and keep it holy, as the Lord your God commanded you.
Work for six days and do all your work.

The seventh day is a Sabbath to the Lord your God. On it you shall do no work—you, your son, your daughter, your male slave, your female slave, your ox, your donkey, any of your livestock, or the resident foreigner in your towns—so that your male slave and your female slave may rest as you do.

Remember that you were a slave in Egypt, and the Lord your God brought you out of there with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm. That is why the Lord your God commanded you to observe the Sabbath day.
Honor your father and your mother, as the Lord your God commanded you, so that your days may be many and things may go well for you in the good land that the Lord your God is giving you.
Do not murder.
Do not commit adultery.
Do not steal.
Do not give false testimony against your neighbor.
Do not covet your neighbor’s wife. Do not covet your neighbor’s house, his field, his vineyard, his male slave, his female slave, his ox, his donkey, or anything that belongs to your neighbor.

The Lord spoke these words to the whole assembly on the mountain, from within the fire, in the cloud and thick darkness, with a mighty voice that had no limit. He wrote them on two stone tablets and gave them to me.
When you heard the voice from within the darkness, while the mountain was blazing with fire, you approached me—all the heads of your tribes and your elders.

You said, “Look, the Lord our God has shown us his glory and his greatness, and we have heard his voice from within the fire. Today we have seen that God can speak with a human being and that person can remain alive.
Now why should we die? This great fire will consume us. If we continue to hear the voice of the Lord our God, we will die.
For what mortal like us has heard the voice of the living God speaking from within the fire and remained alive?
You go near and hear everything the Lord our God says to you. Then tell us everything the Lord our God says to you, and we will listen and do it.”
The Lord heard your words as you spoke to me, and the Lord said to me, “I have heard the voice of this people and the words they have spoken to you. Everything they have said is good.
If only they would always have this heart, to fear me and keep all my commandments, so that things might go well for them and their children forever!
Go and tell them, ‘Return to your tents.’
But you, stand here before me, and I will tell you all my commandments, laws, and judgments, which you are to teach them, so that they may carry them out in the land I am giving them to possess.”
Be careful to do as the Lord your God has commanded you. Do not turn aside to the right or to the left.
Walk in the whole way that the Lord your God has commanded you, so that you may live, things may go well for you, and your days may be many in the land you will possess.
These are the commandments, laws, and judgments that the Lord your God commanded me to teach you, so that you may carry them out in the land you are entering to possess.
You are to fear the Lord your God and keep all his commandments, laws, and judgments that I command you—you, your son, and your grandson—all the days of your life, so that your days may be many.

Listen, Israel, and be careful to obey, so that it may go well with you and you may increase greatly, just as the Lord, the God of your ancestors, promised you, to give you a land flowing with milk and honey.
Listen, Israel: the Lord our God, the Lord is one.
Love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your possessions.
Let these words that I command you today be on your heart.
Repeat them to your children, and speak about them when you sit in your house, when you walk along the road, when you lie down, and when you get up.
Bind them as a sign on your hand, and let them be a mark between your eyes.
Write them on the thresholds of your houses and on your gates.
When the Lord your God brings you into the land that he swore to your ancestors—to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—to give them, giving you large and good towns that you did not build,
And houses filled with every good thing that you did not fill, wells dug that you did not dig, and vineyards and olive trees that you did not plant; and you will eat and be satisfied.
be careful not to forget the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
Fear the Lord your God, serve him, and swear by his name.
Do not follow other gods, the gods of the peoples around you.
For the Lord your God among you is a jealous God. Otherwise, the anger of the Lord your God will blaze against you, and he will destroy you from the face of the earth.
Do not put the Lord your God to the test, as you tested him in the trials.
But keep the commandments of the Lord your God, his testimonies, and his laws that he commanded you.
Do what is good and right before the Lord your God, so that it may go well with you and you may enter and possess the good land that the Lord swore to your ancestors,
and he will crush all your enemies before you, just as the Lord said.
When your son asks you in the future, saying, “What is the meaning of the testimony, the laws, and the judgments that the Lord our God commanded you?”
tell your son, “We were Pharaoh’s slaves in Egypt, and the Lord brought us out of Egypt with a mighty hand.
The Lord performed great and terrible signs and wonders in Egypt, against Pharaoh and all his army, before our eyes.
The Lord brought us out of there to bring us in and give us the land that he swore to our ancestors.
The Lord commanded us to follow all these laws and to fear the Lord our God, so that it might go well with us always and he might keep us alive, as we are today.
It will be righteousness for us if we carefully carry out this whole commandment before the Lord our God, just as he commanded us.”

When the Lord your God brings you into the land that you are entering to possess, and destroys many nations before you—the Hittites, Girgashites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, seven nations more numerous and stronger than you—
and the Lord your God hands them over to you, you must strike them down and utterly destroy them. Do not make a covenant with them or show them mercy.
Do not intermarry with them. Do not give your daughters to their sons or take their daughters for your sons.
So that they do not turn your children away from me, and they serve other gods, and the LORD's anger burns against you and he quickly destroys you.
Instead, do this to them: tear down their altars, break their sacred pillars, cut down their cast images, and burn their carved images with fire.
For you are a people holy to the Lord your God. The Lord your God chose you out of all the peoples on the face of the earth to be his beloved people.
It was not because you were more numerous than all the other peoples that the Lord took pleasure in you and chose you, for you are the smallest of all the peoples.

But because the Lord loves you, and to fulfill the oaths he swore to your ancestors, the Lord brought you out with his mighty hand and redeemed you from the house of slavery, from the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt.
Know that the Lord your God is God, the faithful God, who keeps his covenant and steadfast love for a thousand generations with those who love him and keep his commandments.
He repays those who hate him during their lifetime; he repays them by destroying them. He does not delay with those who hate him, but repays them during their lifetime.
Keep the commandments, laws, and judgments that I command you today, and carry them out.
If you listen to these judgments, keep them, and carry them out, the Lord your God will keep with you the covenant and steadfast love that he swore to your ancestors.

He will love you, bless you, and make you numerous. He will bless the fruit of your womb and the produce of your land, your grain, wine, and oil, the herds of your cattle and the flocks of your sheep, in the land that he swore to your ancestors to give you.
You will be blessed above all peoples. No man or woman among you will be barren, nor will any of your livestock.
The Lord will remove every sickness from you. He will not bring upon you any of the terrible plagues of the Egyptians that you know, but he will bring them upon all who hate you.
You shall devour all the peoples whom the Lord your God gives you. Show them no pity, and do not worship their gods, because they are snares to you.
If you say in your heart, “These nations are more numerous than I am. How can I destroy them?”
Do not be afraid of them. Instead, remember everything that the Lord your God did to Pharaoh and to all Egypt:
the great trials that your eyes saw, the signs and wonders, the mighty hand and uplifted arm. The Lord your God brought you out. The Lord your God will do the same to all the peoples whom you fear.
The Lord your God will also send hornets against them until they perish, including those who remain and those who hide from you.
Do not be afraid of them, because the Lord your God is among you, a great and fearsome God.
The Lord your God will destroy these nations before you little by little. You cannot destroy them quickly, or the wild animals would become too numerous for you.
The Lord your God will deliver them over to you, and you shall strike them with a great blow until you destroy them.
He will deliver their kings into your hands, and you shall wipe out their names from under heaven. No one will stand against you until you have destroyed them.

You shall burn the carved images of their gods in the fire. Do not covet the silver and gold on them or take it for yourself, lest you become defiled by it, because it is detestable before the Lord your God.

Do not bring an unclean thing into your house, so that you do not become devoted to destruction like it. Instead, utterly reject it and regard it as utterly unclean, because it is devoted to destruction.
Keep all the commandments that I command you today, and carry them out, so that you may live, become numerous, enter, and take possession of the land that the Lord swore to your ancestors.

Remember the whole journey on which the Lord your God led you these forty years in the wilderness, to humble you and test you, and to know what was in your hearts, whether you would keep his commandments or not.

He humbled you, let you go hungry, and fed you manna, which neither you nor your ancestors had known, to show you that a person does not live by bread alone, but by everything that comes from the mouth of the Lord.
Your clothes did not wear out on you, and your feet did not go bare these forty years.
Know in your heart that just as a man disciplines his son, so the Lord your God disciplines you.
Keep the commandments of the Lord your God, walk in his ways, and fear him.
For the Lord your God is bringing you into a good land, a land of streams of water, springs, and deep waters flowing out in the valleys and hills;
a land of wheat and barley, vines, fig trees, and pomegranates; a land of olive trees, oil, and honey.
A land where you will not eat bread in poverty and will lack nothing; a land whose stones are iron and from whose mountains you will mine copper.
You will eat and be satisfied, and you will bless the Lord your God for the good land he has given you.
Be careful not to forget the Lord your God. Instead, keep his commandments, his judgments, and his laws that I command you today.
Otherwise, when you eat and are satisfied, and build fine houses and live in them,
and your flocks and cattle multiply, and your silver and gold increase, and everything you have increases,
your heart may become proud, and you may forget the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
He led you through the great and terrifying wilderness, a place of venomous snakes and scorpions, a thirsty place where there was no water. He brought water out of flint rock for you.
He fed you manna in the wilderness, which your ancestors had not known, to humble you and test you, and to do you good in the end.
And you may say in your heart, “By my own power and the strength of my hands I have acquired this wealth.”
Remember the Lord your God, for it is he who gives you the power to acquire wealth, and so confirms his covenant that he swore to your ancestors, as it is today.
If you forget the Lord your God and follow other gods, serve them, and bow down to them, I testify against you today that you will certainly perish.
Like the nations that the Lord destroyed before you, so you will perish if you do not obey the voice of the Lord your God.
Listen, Israel! Today you are crossing the Jordan to go and destroy nations greater and stronger than you, and cities that are great and strong, with walls reaching up to heaven.
They are a great and tall people, descendants of giants, whom you know and about whom you have heard that no one can stand against the giants.

Know today that the Lord your God is crossing ahead of you. He is a consuming fire. He will destroy them and crush them before you, and you will lay them waste and destroy them quickly, as the Lord told you.

When the Lord your God has crushed them before you, do not say in your heart, “Because of my righteousness the Lord brought me in to possess this land.” It is because of the sins of these nations that the Lord is destroying them before you.

It is not because of your righteousness or the uprightness of your heart that you are entering to possess their land. Rather, it is because of the sins of these nations that the LORD your God destroys them before you, and to fulfill the promise he swore to your ancestors, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
Know that it is not because of your righteousness that the Lord your God is giving you this good land to possess, for you are a stubborn people.
Remember, and do not forget, how you provoked the Lord your God to anger in the wilderness. From the day you left Egypt until you came to this place, you have been rebellious before the Lord.
At Horeb you provoked the Lord to anger, and the Lord was angry enough with you to destroy you.

When I went up the mountain and received the stone tablets, the tablets of the covenant that the Lord made with you, I stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights. I ate no bread and drank no water.
The Lord gave me two stone tablets inscribed by the finger of God. On them were all the words that the Lord had spoken to you on the mountain from within the fire on the day of the assembly.
After forty days and forty nights, the Lord gave me the two stone tablets, the tablets of the covenant.

The Lord said to me, “Get up and go down from here quickly, because your people, whom you brought out of Egypt, have become corrupt. They have quickly turned aside from the way I commanded them and have made themselves a cast-metal image.”
The Lord said to me, “I have seen this people, and they are indeed a stubborn people.
Now leave me alone so that I may destroy them and blot out their name from under heaven. I will make you into a nation stronger and more numerous than they are.”
I turned and came down from the mountain. The mountain was blazing with fire, and the two tablets of the covenant were in my two hands.
I saw that you had sinned against the Lord your God and had made yourselves a cast-metal calf. You had quickly turned aside from the way the Lord your God had commanded you.
I took hold of the two tablets, threw them from my two hands, and broke them before your eyes.

I prayed before the Lord as I had before, for forty days and forty nights. I ate no bread and drank no water because of all the sins you had committed, doing evil before the Lord and provoking him to anger.
For I was afraid of the wrath and anger with which the Lord was angry against you, ready to destroy you. But the Lord listened to me that time as well.
The Lord was also very angry with Aaron, ready to destroy him, and I prayed for Aaron too at that time.

I took the calf you had made in your sin and burned it in the fire. I crushed it and ground it thoroughly until it was as fine as dust. Then I threw its dust into the stream flowing down from the mountain.
At Taberah, at Massah, and at Kibroth-hattaavah, you provoked the Lord to anger.

When the Lord sent you from Kadesh-barnea and said to you, “Go up and take possession of the land I have given you,” you rebelled against the command from the Lord’s mouth. You did not believe him or obey his voice.
You have been rebellious before the Lord from the day I came to know you.
I prayed before the Lord for forty days and forty nights because the Lord had said he would destroy you.
I prayed before the LORD and said, 'LORD God, do not destroy your people and your inheritance, whom you redeemed by your greatness and brought out of Egypt with a mighty hand.'
But remember your servants Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Do not look at this people’s stubbornness, wickedness, and sins.

Otherwise, the inhabitants of the land from which you brought them out will say, “Because the Lord did not have the power to bring them into the land he had promised them, and because he hated them, he brought them out to kill them in the wilderness.”
Yet they are your people and your inheritance, whom you brought out by your great power and your uplifted arm.
At that time the Lord said to me, “Cut out two stone tablets like the first ones, and come up to me on the mountain. Make yourself an ark of wood.
I will write on the tablets the words that were on the first tablets, which you broke. Put them in the ark.”
I made an ark of acacia wood and cut two stone tablets like the first ones. I went up the mountain with the two tablets in my hands.

He wrote on the tablets the same writing as before: the Ten Commandments that the Lord had spoken to you on the mountain from within the fire on the day of the assembly. Then the Lord gave them to me.
I turned and came down from the mountain and put the tablets in the ark I had made. I left them in it, as the Lord had commanded me.
The Israelites set out from Beeroth Bene-jaakan for Moserah. There Aaron died and was buried, and his son Eleazar served as priest after him.
From there they set out for Gudgodah, and from Gudgodah for Jotbathah, a land of streams of water.
At that time the Lord set apart the tribe of Levi to carry the ark of the Lord’s covenant, to stand before the Lord and serve him, and to bless the Lord’s name, as they do to this day.
For this reason Levi had no share or inheritance with his brothers, because the Lord is his inheritance, as the Lord your God told him.
I stood before the Lord on the mountain as I had the first time, for forty days and forty nights. The Lord listened to me that time as well, and the Lord was not willing to destroy you.
The LORD said to me, 'Get up, set out, and go ahead of the people, so that they may enter and possess the land that I swore to their ancestors to give them.'
Now, Israel, what does the Lord your God ask of you except to fear the Lord your God, walk in his ways, love him, and serve the Lord your God with all your heart and all your soul,
and to keep the commandments of the Lord your God and his laws that I am commanding you today, so that it may go well with you?
The heavens and the highest heavens, the earth and everything in it, belong to the LORD your God.
Yet the Lord delighted in your ancestors alone and loved them. He chose their descendants after them from among all the peoples, as it is today.
Circumcise the foreskin of your hearts, and no longer stiffen your necks.
For the Lord your God is God of gods and Lord of lords, the great, mighty, and fearsome God, who shows no favoritism and accepts no bribe.
He gives justice to orphans and widows, and loves anyone who turns to him, giving him food and clothing.
Love those who turn to him, because you were foreigners living in the land of Egypt.
Fear the Lord your God, serve him, cling to him, and swear by his name.
For he is your praise, and he is your God, who has done for you these great and fearsome things that your own eyes have seen.
Your ancestors went down to Egypt as seventy people, and now the Lord your God has made you as numerous as the stars in the sky.
Love the LORD your God and keep his requirements, his laws, his judgments, and his commandments all your days.
Know today that it was not for your children, who have not known or seen the discipline of the Lord your God, his greatness, his mighty hand, and his uplifted arm,
and his signs and the deeds he did in Egypt to Pharaoh king of Egypt and to his whole land,

and what he did to the Egyptian army, to the horses, the chariots, and their riders, when he made the waters of the Red Sea flood over them as they pursued you. The Lord destroyed them, and they remain destroyed to this day.
And everything he did for you in the wilderness until you came to this place.

And what he did to Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, the son of Reuben: the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them, their children, their tents, and everything they had, as they stood on their feet among all Israel.
Rather, your own eyes have seen all the great deeds that the Lord has done.
Keep all the commandments that I give you today, so that you may be strong and go in and take possession of the land you are crossing over to possess,
and so that you may live long in the land that the Lord swore to your ancestors to give them and their descendants, a land flowing with milk and honey.
For the land you are entering to possess is not like the land of Egypt, from which you came, where you sowed your seed and watered it with your feet like an irrigated garden.
But the land you are crossing over to possess is a land of mountains and valleys, which drinks water from the rain of heaven.
It is a land that the Lord your God constantly cares for. The eyes of the Lord your God are on it from the beginning of the year to the end of the year.
If you obey the commandments that I give you today, love the Lord your God, and serve him with all your heart and all your soul,
I will give rain for your land in its season, the early rain and the late rain, and you will gather your grain, your wine, and your oil.
I will give grass in your fields for your livestock, and you will eat and be satisfied.
Be careful that your hearts are not deceived, and that you do not turn aside, serve other gods, and bow down to them.

Then the Lord's anger will burn against you, and he will shut up the sky so that there is no rain, and the land will not yield its crops. You will quickly perish from the good land that the Lord your God is giving you.
Place these commandments in your hearts and souls. Bind them as a sign on your hands, and let them be a mark between your eyes.
Teach them to your children so that they speak of them when you sit in your houses, when you walk along the road, when you lie down, and when you get up.
Write them on the thresholds of your houses and on your gates.
So that your days and the days of your children may be many in the land that the Lord your God swore to your ancestors to give them, as long as the heavens remain above the earth.
If you keep all these commandments that I command you today and carry them out, love the Lord your God, walk in all his ways, and hold fast to him,
the Lord will destroy all these nations before you, and you will dispossess nations greater and stronger than you.
Every place where the sole of your foot treads will be yours. From the wilderness and Lebanon, and from the river to the river Euphrates, and as far as the western sea will be your territory.
No one will stand against you. The Lord your God will spread fear and dread of you over the whole land where you tread, as the Lord told you.
See, I am setting blessings and curses before you today:
blessings if you obey the commandments of the Lord your God that I command you today,
and curses if you do not obey the commandments of the Lord your God, if you turn aside from the way that I command you today and follow other gods whom you do not know.
When the Lord your God brings you into the land that you are entering to possess, pronounce the blessings on Mount Gerizim and the curses on Mount Ebal.
They are beyond the Jordan, behind the road toward the setting sun, in the land of the Canaanites who live in the Arabah, opposite Gilgal and opposite the site of the oak of Mamre.
For you are crossing the Jordan to enter and possess the land that the Lord your God is giving you. You will possess it and live in it.
Keep and carry out all the laws and judgments that I am setting before you today.
These are the laws and judgments that you must keep and carry out in the land that the Lord, the God of your ancestors, is giving you to possess, all the days that you live on the earth.
Destroy all the places where the nations you are dispossessing worshiped their gods, on the high mountains, on the hills, and under every tree that gives shade.
Tear down their altars, break their sacred pillars, burn their cast images with fire, and break their carved gods. Wipe out their names from that place.
You must not worship the Lord your God in this way.
Instead, seek out his dwelling place at the place that the Lord your God chooses from all your tribes to put his name there, and go there.
Bring there your whole burnt offerings, your sacrifices, your tithes, the contributions from your hands, your vowed offerings, your offerings, and the firstborn of your cattle and your flocks.
Eat there before the Lord your God, and rejoice in everything you undertake, you and the members of your households, because the Lord your God has blessed you.
You must not do as we are doing here today, each person doing what seems right in his own eyes.
For you have not yet reached the resting place and the inheritance that the Lord your God is giving you.
Cross the Jordan and settle in the land that the Lord your God is giving you as an inheritance. He will give you rest from all your enemies around you, and you will live in safety.

To the place that the Lord your God chooses for his name to dwell, bring everything that I command you: your whole burnt offerings, your sacrifices, your tithes, the contributions from your hands, and all the choice offerings that you vow to the Lord.
Rejoice before the LORD your God—you, your sons and daughters, your male and female slaves, and the Levites in your towns—because they have no inheritance or share with you.
Be careful not to offer your whole burnt offering wherever you please.
But only at the place the Lord chooses in one of your tribes shall you offer your whole burnt offerings. There you shall do everything I command you.

However, you may slaughter animals and eat meat whenever you wish, according to the blessing the Lord your God gives you, in any of your towns. Both the unclean and the clean may eat it, as they would a gazelle or a deer.
Only you must not eat the blood. Pour it out on the ground like water.

You are not permitted to eat in your towns the tithes of your grain, wine, and oil, the firstborn of your cattle and flocks, any of the offerings you vow to give, your offerings, or the contributions from your hands.

Instead, you shall eat them before the Lord your God, at the place the Lord your God chooses for himself—you, your son and daughter, your male and female slaves, and the Levite in your towns. You shall rejoice before the Lord your God in everything you undertake.
Be careful not to neglect the Levites for as long as you live in the land.
When the Lord your God enlarges your territory as he promised you, and you say, “I will eat meat,” because you crave meat, you may eat meat whenever you wish.

If the place the Lord your God chooses to put his name there is far from you, slaughter animals from the cattle and flocks the Lord your God gives you, as he commanded you, and eat in your towns whenever you wish.
But you shall eat it just as a gazelle or a deer is eaten. The unclean and the clean may eat it together.
Only be firm in not eating the blood, because the blood is the life. You must not eat the life with the meat.
You must not eat it. Pour it out on the ground like water.
You must not eat it, so that it may go well with you and your children after you, when you do what is right before the Lord your God.
But take the holy offerings you have and your vowed offerings, and come to the place the Lord chooses.
Offer your whole burnt offering, both flesh and blood, on the altar of the Lord your God. The blood of your sacrifices shall be poured out on the altar of the Lord your God, but you may eat the meat.
Keep and obey all these commandments that I give you today, so that it may go well with you and your children after you forever, when you do what is good and right before the Lord your God.
When the LORD your God destroys the nations to whom you are going, and destroys them before you, and you take possession of them and settle in their land.

Be careful not to go astray by following them after the Lord destroys them before you. Do not inquire about their gods, saying, “How did these nations worship their gods? I will do the same as they did.”
You must not worship the Lord your God in that way, because they did for their gods everything the Lord rejects and hates. They even burned their sons and daughters in the fire for their gods.
Be careful to carry out every command that I give you. Do not add to it or take away from it.
When a prophet or a dreamer of dreams arises among you and gives you a sign and a wonder,
and the sign and wonder he told you about come to pass, and he says to you, “Come, let us follow other gods whom you have not known, and let us worship them,”
do not listen to the words of that prophet or that dreamer of dreams, because the Lord your God is testing you to know whether you love the Lord your God with all your heart and all your soul.
Follow the Lord your God, fear him, keep his commandments, obey him, serve him, and hold fast to him.

That prophet or that dreamer of dreams shall be put to death, because he has spoken wickedly against the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt and redeemed you from the house of slavery, to lead you astray from the path the Lord your God commanded you to follow. You shall remove the evil from among you.

If your brother, your mother's son, or your son or daughter, or the wife of your covenant, or your friend who is like your own soul, secretly entices you, saying, “Come, let us go and worship other gods whom neither you nor your ancestors have known,”
from among the gods of the peoples around you, whether near you or far from you, from one end of the earth to the other,
do not be persuaded by him or listen to him. Do not look on him with pity, show him mercy, or shield him.
But you must certainly kill him. Your hand must be the first against him to kill him, and afterward the hand of all the people.
Stone him to death, because he tried to lead you astray from the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
All the house of Israel will hear and be afraid, and they will never again do such an evil thing among you.
When you hear in one of your towns that the Lord your God is giving you to live in, and people tell you,
“Wicked men have gone out from among you and led the people of their town astray, saying, ‘Let us go and serve other gods whom you have not known,’”
investigate, examine, and inquire carefully. If the report is indeed true, and this abomination has been committed among you,
destroy the inhabitants of that town with the sword. Destroy it and everything in it, including its livestock, with the sword.
Gather all its plunder into its public square, and burn the town and all its plunder completely with fire before the Lord your God. It must remain a mound of ruins forever and never be rebuilt.

Nothing devoted to destruction must remain in your hand, so that the Lord may turn from his fierce anger, grant you mercy, have compassion on you, love you, and make you numerous, as he swore to your ancestors,
if you obey the voice of the Lord your God, keep his commandments that I am commanding you today, and do what is right before the Lord your God.
You are children of the Lord your God. Do not cut yourselves or make bald patches between your eyes for the dead.
For you are a people holy to the Lord your God. The Lord your God has chosen you to be his dearly beloved people above all the peoples on the face of the earth.
Do not eat anything unclean.
These are the animals you may eat: the ox, the lamb, the ewe, and the goat;
the deer, the gazelle, the fallow deer, the ibex, the wild ox, the antelope, and the mountain sheep.
You may eat any animal whose hoof is split and divided in two and that chews the cud.

But among those that chew the cud and those whose hooves are split into separate parts, you must not eat these: the camel, the hare, and the rock badger. They chew the cud, but their hooves are not split; they are unclean for you.
The pig, whose hoof is split but which does not chew the cud, is unclean for you. Do not eat their meat or approach their carcasses.
These you may eat from everything in the water: eat anything that has fins and scales.
Do not eat anything that does not have fins and scales; it is unclean for you.
You may eat any clean bird.
But these are the ones you must not eat: the eagle;
the kite;
the raven, in its various kinds;
the ostrich and the hawk, in their various kinds;
the owl and the [?].
And the pelican and the roller.
And the stork and the heron according to their kinds, and the wild rooster and the peacock.
All the offspring of these flying creatures are unclean for you. They must not be eaten.
You may eat any clean flying creature.

Do not eat anything unclean. Instead, give it to the resident alien in your towns to eat, or sell it to a foreigner, because you are a people holy to the Lord your God. Do not cook a young goat in its mother's milk.
Be sure to set aside a tenth of all the produce of your seed that the field yields year after year.

Eat before the Lord your God, in the place he chooses for his name to dwell there, the tithes of your grain, wine, and oil, and the firstborn of your cattle and flocks, so that you may learn to fear the Lord your God all your days.
If the journey is too long for you and you cannot carry it, because the place the Lord your God chooses for his name to dwell there is far from you, when the Lord your God has blessed you,
sell it for money, tie up the money in your hand, and go to the place the Lord your God chooses.
With the money, buy whatever you desire: cattle, sheep, wine, strong drink, or anything else you wish for. Eat there before the Lord your God, and rejoice, you and your household.
Do not abandon the Levite in your towns, because he has no share or inheritance with you.
At the end of three years, bring out the entire tithe of your produce for that year and leave it in your towns.

Then the Levite, who has no share or inheritance with you, anyone who turns to me, and the orphan and widow in your towns may come, eat, and be satisfied. And the Lord your God will bless you in all the work your hands do.
At the end of seven years, grant a release from debts.

This is the rule for the release: every creditor must cancel the debt his neighbor owes him. He must not demand payment from his neighbor or his brother, because a release has been proclaimed for the Lord.
You may demand payment from a foreigner, but you must cancel whatever your brother owes you.
There should be no poor person among you, because the Lord your God will surely bless you in the land the Lord your God is giving you to inherit,
if you obey the voice of the Lord your God and carefully carry out this entire commandment that I am giving you today.
The Lord your God will bless you as he told you. You will lend to many nations, but you will not borrow. You will rule over many nations, but they will not rule over you.
If there is a poor person among you, one of your brothers, in one of your towns in the land the Lord your God is giving you, do not harden your heart or close your hand against your poor brother.
Instead, open your hand to him and lend him whatever he lacks.

Be careful that no wicked thought enters your heart, and you say, 'The year of release, the sabbatical year, is near,' and you look grudgingly at your poor brother and give him nothing. He may cry out to the Lord against you, and you will be guilty of sin.
Instead, give to him, and do not be resentful when you give to him. Because of this, the Lord your God will bless you in all your work and in everything you undertake.
For the poor will never disappear from the land. That is why I command you and tell you to open your hand to your poor brother and to the needy in your land.
When your fellow Hebrew, whether a man or a woman, is sold to you, that person shall serve you for six years. In the seventh year, set that person free to leave you.
When you release him from your service as a free man, do not send him away empty-handed.
Instead, set aside provisions and give them to him from your flocks and your cattle, from your threshing floor and your winepress. Give to him from what the Lord your God has given you.
Remember that you were a slave in Egypt and that the Lord your God redeemed you. That is why I am giving you this command today.
But if he says to you, 'I will not leave you, because I love you and your household, and I am well off with you,'
Take an awl and pierce his ear against the door, and he will be your slave forever. Do the same for your female slave.
Do not resent setting him free and sending him away from you, because he has served you for six years for twice the wages of a hired worker. The Lord your God will bless you in everything you do.
Consecrate to the Lord your God every firstborn male born among your cattle and your flock. Do not work the firstborn of your cattle or shear the firstborn of your flock.
Instead, eat it before the Lord your God year after year, you and your household, in the place the Lord chooses.
But if it has a defect—if it is lame or blind or has any other objectionable condition—do not offer it to the Lord your God.
Instead, eat it in your towns. The unclean and the clean alike may eat it, as you would a gazelle or a deer.
Only you must not eat the blood. Pour it out on the ground like water.
Observe the month of blossoms and celebrate the Passover to the Lord your God, because in the month of blossoms the Lord your God brought you out of Egypt by night.
Slaughter the Passover sacrifice to the Lord your God from the flock and the cattle, in the place the Lord your God chooses for his name to dwell there.

Do not eat leavened bread with it. Instead, for seven days eat unleavened bread with it, the bread of affliction, because you came out of Egypt in haste, so that you may remember the day you came out of Egypt all the days of your life.
No leaven is to be seen anywhere within your territory for seven days. None of the meat you slaughter on the evening of the first day is to remain overnight until morning.
You are not permitted to slaughter the Passover sacrifice in any of your towns that the Lord your God gives you.
Instead, slaughter the Passover sacrifice in the place the Lord your God chooses for his name to dwell, in the evening at sunset, at the time when you came out of Egypt.
Cook it and eat it in the place the Lord your God chooses for himself. Then turn back in the morning and go to your tent.
For six days you must eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day there is to be an assembly for the Lord your God. You must do no work on it.
Count seven weeks for yourself. Begin counting the seven weeks when you first put the sickle to the standing grain.
Celebrate the Festival of Weeks to the Lord your God with an offering that you set apart from your own hands, in proportion to how the Lord your God has blessed you.

Rejoice before the Lord your God—you, your son and daughter, your male and female slaves, the Levite in your towns, and the foreign resident, the orphan, and the widow among you—in the place the Lord your God chooses for his name to dwell there.
Remember that you were a slave in Egypt. Keep and carry out all these laws.
Celebrate the Festival of Shelters for seven days when you gather in the produce from your threshing floor and your winepress.
Rejoice at your festival—you, your son and daughter, your male and female slaves, and the Levite, the orphan, the widow, and the foreign resident in your towns.

Celebrate a festival to the Lord your God for seven days in the place the Lord chooses, so that the Lord your God may bless you in all your produce and in all the work of your hands, and you will be joyful.

Three times a year all your males must appear before the Lord your God in the place he chooses: at the Festival of Unleavened Bread, the Festival of Weeks, and the Festival of Shelters. Do not appear before the Lord your God empty-handed.
Instead, each person must bring a gift according to what his hand can give, in proportion to the blessing the Lord your God has given you.
Appoint judges and scribes for your tribes in all your towns that the Lord your God gives you, and they must judge the people with righteous judgments.
Do not pervert justice, show partiality, or accept a bribe, because a bribe blinds the eyes of the wise in judgment and distorts the words of the innocent.
Instead, judge your neighbor fairly, so that you may live and enter and inherit the land that the Lord your God is giving you.
Do not plant saplings of any kind of tree beside the altar of the Lord your God that you make for yourself.
Do not set up a sacred pillar for yourself, something the Lord your God hates.
Do not sacrifice to the Lord your God an ox or a sheep that has a defect or anything detestable about it, because it is unclean before the Lord your God.
If there is found among you, in one of your towns that the Lord your God is giving you, a man or woman who does what is evil before the Lord your God and violates his covenant,
and goes and serves other gods and bows down to them, or to the sun or the moon or any of the heavenly hosts, which I have not commanded,
and you are told about it and hear of it, investigate thoroughly. If the report is true and this abomination has been committed in Israel,
bring out that man or woman who has done this evil deed in your towns, whether a man or a woman, and stone them to death.
On the testimony of two witnesses or three witnesses, the person liable to death shall be put to death. No one shall be put to death on the testimony of one witness.
The witnesses must be the first to raise their hands against that person to put him to death, and afterward all the people. You must destroy the evildoers from among you.

When a judicial matter is too difficult for you—distinguishing between one case of bloodshed and another, between one legal case and another, or between one leprous sore and another—a disputed matter in your towns, get up and go to the place that the Lord your God will choose for himself.
Go to the priest and the Levite, or to the judge who is in office in those days, and inquire. They will tell you the judicial decision.
Act according to the decision they give you from that place, as the Lord has said. Be careful to do as they instruct you.
Act according to the law they explain to you and the judgment they pronounce to you. Do not turn aside from the decision they give you, either to the right or to the left.
The man who acts arrogantly and refuses to obey the priest who stands there to serve before the Lord your God, or the judge, shall be put to death. You must destroy the evildoers from Israel.
All the people will hear and be afraid, and they will no longer act arrogantly.
When you enter the land that the Lord your God is giving you, inherit it, and settle in it, and you say, “I will appoint a king over me like these nations around me,”

you must indeed appoint over you a king whom the Lord your God chooses. Appoint a king over you from among your own brothers. You are not permitted to appoint a foreigner over you, someone who is not one of your brothers.
But he must not acquire many horses for himself, lest the people be taken back to Egypt to increase his horses. The Lord has told you, “You must never return by this way again.”
He must not take many wives for himself, lest they turn his heart aside, and he must not accumulate excessive silver and gold for himself.
When he sits on the throne of his kingdom, he must write for himself in a book a copy of this law, from the one kept before the priest and the Levite.
It must remain with him, and he must read it all the days of his life, so that he may learn to fear the Lord his God and keep all the words of this law and these commandments and carry them out.

Then his heart will not be lifted up above his brothers, and he will not turn aside from the commandments, either to the right or to the left, so that he and his sons may reign for many days among the Israelites.
The priest and the Levite shall have no share or inheritance among the Israelites. Instead, they shall eat the offerings of the Lord and his inheritance.
He shall have no inheritance among his brothers, for the LORD is his inheritance, as he told him.
This shall be the priest’s due from the people, from those who slaughter an animal, whether an ox or a sheep: they shall give the priest the shoulder, the cheek, and the stomach.
Give him the first of your grain, your wine, and your oil, and the first wool sheared from your sheep.
For the LORD your God has chosen him out of all your tribes to stand and serve in the name of the LORD your God, he and his sons for all time.
If a Levite, one of your brothers from anywhere in Israel, comes from the place where he lives, he may come with all his heart’s desire to the place the LORD chooses.
He shall serve in the name of the LORD his God, like all his fellow Levites who stand there before the LORD.
They shall eat equal portions, apart from the proceeds of selling ancestral property.
When you enter the land that the LORD your God is giving you, do not learn to act according to the practices of those nations.

There must not be found among you anyone who makes his son or daughter pass through fire, anyone who practices divination, anyone who performs illusions, anyone who interprets omens, or anyone who practices sorcery.
Or one who practices magic with spells, or one who consults mediums and spiritists, or consults the dead.
For everyone who does these things is unclean before the LORD your God, and because of these abominations the LORD your God is destroying them before you.
Be blameless before the LORD your God.
For these nations that you are dispossessing listen to mediums and diviners. But the LORD your God has not permitted you to do so.
The LORD your God will raise up for himself a prophet like me from among you, from your brothers. You must listen to him.

This is according to what you asked of the LORD your God at Horeb on the day of the assembly, when you said, ‘Let me no longer hear the voice of the LORD my God or see this great fire again, so that I do not die.’
And the LORD said to me, ‘Everything they have said is good.
I will raise up for them a prophet like you from among their brothers. I will put my words in his mouth, and he will tell them everything I command him.
Anyone who does not listen to my words that he speaks in my name—I myself will call him to account.
But a prophet who presumes to speak a word in my name that I have not commanded him to say, or who speaks in the name of other gods—that prophet shall be put to death.’
If you say in your heart, ‘How can I recognize a word that the LORD has not spoken?’
When a prophet speaks in the name of the LORD and the word does not happen or come true, that is a word the LORD has not spoken. The prophet has spoken it presumptuously. Do not be afraid of him.
When the LORD your God destroys the nations whose land the LORD your God is giving you, and you dispossess them and live in their towns and houses,
set apart three towns for yourself within your land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance.
Prepare the road and divide the territory of the land that the LORD your God gives you as an inheritance into three parts, so that anyone who kills someone may flee there.
This is the right of someone who kills his neighbor and may remain alive: he must have killed his neighbor unintentionally, without having hated him previously.

If someone goes into the forest with his neighbor to cut wood, and raises his hand with the axe to cut the wood, and the iron head slips off the handle and strikes his neighbor so that he dies, that person may flee to one of these towns and live.

Otherwise, the avenger of blood might pursue the killer in the heat of his anger, overtake him because the journey is long, and kill him, although he does not deserve a death sentence, since he had not previously hated the other man.
That is why I command you and tell you to set apart three towns for yourselves.
When the Lord your God enlarges your territory, as he swore to your ancestors, and gives you all the land he swore to your ancestors to give you,
if you keep and carry out all these commandments that I give you today—to love the Lord your God and to walk in his ways all your days—then you must add three more towns to these three.
This is so that innocent blood will not be shed in your land, which the Lord your God is giving you, and bloodguilt will not be charged against you.
But if a man hates his neighbor, lies in wait for him, attacks him and strikes him so that he dies, and then flees to one of these towns,
the elders of his town must send for him, bring him back from there, and hand him over to the avenger of blood to be put to death.
Do not pity him, but put him to death. Avenge Israel’s innocent blood, so that things may go well for you.
Do not move the ancient boundary marker that your predecessors set up in the inheritance you will receive in the land that the Lord your God is giving you to possess.
A single witness is not sufficient to convict a person of any offense or any sin, whatever sin he may commit. A matter must be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses.
If a false witness comes forward against a man and testifies against him about wrongdoing,
both men involved in the dispute must stand before the Lord and before the priest and the judge who are serving at that time.
The judges must investigate thoroughly and see whether he was seeking to give false testimony against his brother.
Do to him as he intended to do to his brother. Remove the evil from among you.
Those who remain will hear and be afraid, and they will never again do such an evil thing among you.
Show no pity: life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.

When you go out to battle against your enemies and see horses and chariots and an army larger than yours, do not be afraid of them, because the Lord your God, who brought you up from the land of Egypt, goes with you.
When you approach the battle, the priest must come forward and speak to the people.
Listen, Israel! Today you are approaching battle against your enemies. Do not lose heart or be afraid. Do not tremble or panic before them.
For the Lord your God, who brought you up from the land of Egypt, goes with you. He will fight for you against your enemies and save you.
The officers must say to the people, “Who has built a new house but has not dedicated it? Let him go back home, so that he does not die in battle and another man dedicate it.
And who has planted a vineyard but has not pressed wine from it? Let him go back home, so that he does not die in battle and another man press its wine.
And who has become engaged to a woman but has not married her? Let him go back home, so that he does not die in battle and another man marry her.”
The officers must continue speaking to the people and say, “Who is afraid and trembling at heart? Let him go back home, so that his brothers do not lose heart as he has.”
When the officers have finished speaking to the people, the commanders of the armies must take their places at the head of the people.
When you approach a town to fight against it, offer it peace.
If it answers you peacefully and opens its gates to you, all the people found in it shall become your tribute-paying servants and serve you.
But if it does not make peace with you and wages war against you, besiege it.
The Lord your God will hand it over to you, and you shall kill all its males with the sword.
But take the women, the children, the livestock, everything in the town, and all its plunder for yourself. Enjoy the plunder of your enemies that the Lord your God gives you.
Do this to all the towns very far from you that do not belong to these peoples.
But in the towns of these peoples that the Lord your God gives you as an inheritance, leave nothing that breathes alive.
Instead, destroy them completely—the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites—as the Lord your God commanded you.
This is so that they will not teach you to practice all the detestable things they used to do for their gods, and so cause you to sin against the Lord your God.

When you besiege a town for many days, fighting against it to capture it, do not destroy its trees or use an iron tool against them. You eat from them—would you cut them down? For a tree in the field is not like a human being who can flee from you during a siege.
But a tree that you know is not a food-producing tree you may destroy and cut down. Build siegeworks against the town that is waging war against you until you capture it.
When someone who has been killed is found lying in a field in the land that the Lord your God gives you to possess, and it is not known who killed him,
your elders and judges shall go out and measure the distances to the towns surrounding the dead man.
The elders of the town nearest the dead man shall take a heifer from the herd that has never been worked and has never pulled a yoke.
The elders of that town shall bring the heifer down to an uncultivated valley that has neither been worked nor sown, and there in the valley they shall slaughter the heifer.

The priests, the descendants of Levi, shall come forward, because the Lord your God has chosen them to serve him and to bless in the Lord’s name. Every dispute and every case of injury shall be settled by their word.
All the elders of that town who are nearest the dead man shall wash their hands over the heifer slaughtered in the valley.
They shall declare, “Our hands did not shed this blood, and our eyes did not see it.
Forgive your people Israel, whom you redeemed, Lord, and do not hold your people Israel accountable for innocent blood.” Then they shall be forgiven for the bloodshed.
You shall investigate the shedding of innocent blood among you and do what is right before the Lord your God.
When you go out to war against your enemies and the Lord your God hands them over to you, and you take captives from among them,
and you see among the captives a beautiful woman whom you desire and take as your wife,
you shall bring her into your house. She shall shave her head and trim her nails.

She shall take off the clothes she wore as a captive and stay in your house, mourning her father and mother for a full month. Afterward you may sleep with her and marry her, and she shall be your wife.
If you do not want her, let her go free. Do not sell her for money or trade her, because you have humiliated her.
When a man has two wives, one loved and the other hated, and both the loved wife and the hated wife bear him sons, but the firstborn son belongs to the hated wife,
then, when he gives his sons their inheritance from what he owns, he may not give the loved wife’s son the rights of the firstborn ahead of the hated wife’s son.
